n: After Assyria’s great “forest” is cut down (chapter 20), a new shoot grows from the stump of Jesse, King David’s father. Latter-day revelation identifies the “stem of Jesse” as Christ. The angel Moroni quoted this chapter to Joseph Smith, saying it was about to be fulfilled.

f.g: A shoot or twig. D&C 113:3-4 describes it as a servant in Christ’s hands.

n: The Spirit of the Lord will rest on Him with wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and reverence for the Lord — the full gifts of the Spirit.

f.w: the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him

n: He delights in reverence for God, and He will not judge by appearances or hearsay, but by perfect understanding.

f.w: he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes

n: He will judge the poor fairly and defend the meek. His word — “the rod of his mouth” and “breath of his lips” — will strike the earth and destroy the wicked.
Righteousness and faithfulness will be like the belt around His waist — always with Him, ready for action.
A vision of the Millennium: predators and prey live together in peace — wolf with lamb, leopard with goat, lion with calf — and a child leads them.

f.w: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb

n: Cows and bears graze together, their young lie down side by side, and lions eat straw like oxen. Even nature will be transformed.

f.w: the lion shall eat straw like the ox

n: Babies will play near cobra holes, and toddlers will put their hands in a viper’s den without harm.

f.g: A venomous snake, such as a cobra.
A venomous snake or viper (KJV used a mythical creature name).

n: No one will hurt or destroy in God’s holy mountain, for the earth will be full of knowledge of the Lord, as the oceans are full of water.

f.w: the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord

n: The “root of Jesse” will stand as a banner to the peoples, and the Gentiles will seek Him. Latter-day revelation describes this root as a descendant of Jesse and Joseph holding priesthood keys for the gathering.

The Lord will reach out “a second time” to recover His people — the first was the Exodus. He will gather the remnant from Assyria, Egypt, Ethiopia, Persia, Babylon, and distant lands. This is the latter-day gathering of Israel.

f.g: Ethiopia/Sudan region. Elam = western Persia; Shinar = Babylonia.

n: He will raise a banner for the nations and gather Israel’s outcasts and Judah’s scattered people from the four corners of the earth.

f.w: set up an ensign for the nations

n: Ancient rivalry between Ephraim (the northern kingdom) and Judah will end. They will no longer envy or harass one another.
United, Israel will overcome old enemies — Philistines to the west, peoples of the east, Edom, Moab, and Ammon. These traditional foes symbolize all who oppose God’s people.

f.g: Neighboring nations east and south of Israel, often hostile.

n: The Lord will dry up the “tongue” (gulf) of the Egyptian sea and divide the river (the Euphrates) into seven streams so people can cross on dry ground — a new Exodus.

f.g: With dry sandals — on dry ground.

n: There will be a highway for the returning remnant, just as there was for Israel coming out of Egypt.
